passages.original: Satis ista de terrae nomine, in quo materiam intellegi voluit, quod nomen unius elementi omnes sciunt, natura primum, dehinc scriptura docente; nisi si et Sileno illi apud Midam regem adseveranti de alio orbe credendum est, auctore Theopompo. Sed et deos multos idem refert.
passages.english: Enough of this about the name "earth", under which he wanted matter to be understood, when everyone knows it as the name of a single element, taught first by nature and then by Scripture; unless we are also to believe that famous Silenus, who, on the authority of Theopompus, asserted before King Midas [the existence] of another world. But the same [writer] also reports many gods.
passages.notes: "Idem refert" may refer either to Theopompus or to Silenus; taken here as the writer reporting, though it could mean Silenus speaks of many gods. The story is Theopompus' account of Silenus telling Midas of a continent beyond the known world.
